summary: Fractional tokenization micro-charges observed after tokenizer upgrade impacting hourly metering
description:
Issue summary:
NeuroCart reports a set of small, recurring micro-charges on their weekly invoice that started immediately after our tokenizer service was upgraded on 2026-03-09. Charges appear as fractional token units (~0.001–0.02 token deltas) across many short requests, aggregated into a visible provisional line on their account.

Impact:
- Customer saw ~150 small charge-line entries totalling $18.35 on a provisional invoice for the window 2026-03-09 00:00 - 2026-03-10 06:00 UTC.
- Affects production traffic in us-west only. No functional regressions reported in model outputs.
- Customer is concerned about overbilling due to rounding behavior after tokenizer update.

Environment:
- Private enterprise account routed through hosted metering postback (prod, us-west).
- Tokenizer service rolled to v2.4.0 on 2026-03-09 01:12 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (reported by customer):
1) Run many small chat requests (20–80 bytes) from NeuroCart staging harness using API key K-****-NC.
2) Observe per-request token counts in response headers (x-rc-tokens).
3) Aggregate reported tokens over hourly window; floats present (e.g., 0.005, 0.012) rather than integer token counts expected.
4) Check account provisional invoice and see many micro-line entries.

Observed logs and headers (attached by customer):
- Sample response headers: x-rc-tokens: "1.012", "0.988", "1.005"
- Postback payloads show token_count field as floats in some entries: token_count: 1.005
- Postback timestamps align with tokenizer deployment time.

Customer request:
- Please confirm whether these are valid charges and whether we should credit the micro-amounts. They request a provisional hold and a short-term waiver if this is a platform-side billing artifact.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:21 - Maya Chen (Support): Acknowledged the report, opened ticket with billing and infra. Asked customer for request IDs and sample postbacks (received 09:34).

2026-03-10 11:05 - Liam O'Neill (SRE): Noted tokenizer rollout at 2026-03-09 01:12 UTC and a change in tokenizer fractional accounting in v2.4.0. Added 'tokenizer' and 'postback-processor' to components.

2026-03-11 08:17 - SRE (Liam): Initial hypothesis: tokenizer produced fractional token weights for edge-case Unicode sequences; metering pipeline expected integers but tolerated floats and aggregated them. Possible rounding policy change in metering step. Created PR to add defensive rounding in postback ingest. See PR #892.
2026-03-12 10:03 - Support (Maya): Updated customer. Requested permission to apply provisional credit pending investigation (customer agreed).
2026-03-13 16:30 - Billing Ops (Zainab): Applied temporary provisional credit of $18.35 to NeuroCart account while investigation completes (credit_id: CR-2026-03-13-420789).
investigation_notes: Found regression in tokenizer v2.4.0: certain multi-byte punctuation sequences returned token weights as floats (weight aggregation logic changed in tokenizer rewrite).
Metering ingest accepted token_count as float; upstream aggregator summed floats into decimal totals without applying floor/ceil policy (expected integer rounding at tokenization boundary).
Edge-case sequence pattern: "\u201c\u201d" + zero-width joiner triggered fractional weight 0.005–0.02 in about 0.4% of short requests from NeuroCart traffic profile.
Postback-processor schema allows numeric token_count; no validation error. Need a schema enforcement or ingest-time rounding to match billing policy.
Related: INT-331 shows a separate internal alert where rounding policy was discussed during metering refactor (May 2025).
root_cause: Tokenizer v2.4.0 introduced fractional token weights for a small class of multi-byte sequences. Metering pipeline accepted floats and aggregated them, producing micro-charge entries instead of applying integer rounding per token as billing expects.
action_items: Roll back tokenizer change for fractional weights to v2.3.7 in us-west (rollback scheduled 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC) or apply hotfix to enforce integer tokenization boundaries.
Patch postback-processor to apply billing rounding policy at ingest (floor token counts to nearest integer consistently) — PR #892 opened.
Create automated unit test for tokenizer to prevent future fractional weights for discrete tokens.
Issue credit to customer for provisional amount and reconcile final invoice after fix. (credit CR-2026-03-13-420789 applied)
resolution: 2026-03-14 03:10 - SRE: Rolled forward hotfix v2.4.1 to tokenizer that snaps token weights to integer boundaries for the affected sequences. Verified no float token_count emitted in sampled traffic over 2 hours.

2026-03-14 04:00 - Billing Ops: Confirmed provisional credit of $18.35 will remain and will be converted to a permanent invoice credit once the next billing reconciliation completes. Customer notified.

2026-03-14 08:20 - Support (Maya): Sent formal apology and short postmortem to NeuroCart; included mitigation steps and timeline. Customer accepted credit and flagged for follow-up on a post-deployment billing audit.
Follow-up: Add a monitoring alert for token_count floats in postbacks (owner: SRE/infrastructure). Add acceptance test to CI for tokenizer-based metering (owner: Tokenizer team).
